symbol_repair_2026_11_07.why: docx_text() dropped characters Word writes as Symbol-font w:sym elements. cth_convert_sym_v8.py maps them to Unicode (Symbol F0BE —, F0B7 •, F0B4 × and the like), Wingdings boxes to "[ ]", and private-use code points U+F0xx the same way; run with its mapping switched off it reproduces the first deposit byte for byte.
symbol_repair_2026_11_07.what_changed: A diff against the first deposit shows only these 5 lines changed (same 1,910 lines, 5 characters more), each one em dash (Symbol F0BE -> —) restored: lines 673 and 674, s 44(4) definition of 'value', paragraphs (a) and (b): 'damage to the property—the indemnity value of the property' and 'replacement of the property—the reinstatement or replacement value of the property'; lines 838, 839 and 840, s 59(2A) definition of 'applicable business day': 'because of section 58—the fourteenth business day', 'otherwise—the third business day', 'a contract of life insurance—the twentieth business day'. Line numbers are unchanged, so the formulas sidecar's references still hold.
symbol_repair_2026_11_07.encodings_affected: baseline-2026-10 relies on s 44(4) (the @desc of 'the value of the property' in the s 44(2), (3) rule) and s 59(2A) (the rule 'On which business day can a cancellation take effect', 14 / 3 / 20 business days); both were read correctly from the broken text (the s 59(2A) quotation already supplies the dashes as ' -- '), so no rule, case, value or finding changed; no encoding records the text hash
